pages.title: EV Charging in Egypt: Tariffs and 45 °C Sites | Anari
pages.meta: How to build EV charging in Egypt: the 0.45/0.80 regulated resale markup, GOEIC import conformity, and why 45 °C ambient decides the charger you specify.
pages.h1: EV charging in Egypt: regulated tariffs, 45 °C design, grid access
pages.lede: Egypt sets the resale margin by decree, so revenue per kWh is known before the first site is signed. What separates a working site from a stalled one is the grid connection offer, the design ambient temperature and the import conformity path.
pages.tldr: Resale margin is fixed by Decision 101/2025: supply tariff plus 0.45 on AC and 0.80 on DC. Secure the connection offer first, specify for 45 °C in Upper Egypt, and clear GOEIC import conformity before shipment.
sections: What the regulated margin means for your model

Because the DC markup over the supply tariff is fixed at 0.80 by decree, a CPO in Egypt does not price the kWh — the state does. The business case therefore moves to utilisation: sessions per gun per day, uptime in summer, and how many vehicles one grid connection can serve. A three-gun DC layout on a single feeder raises revenue per available kilowatt without needing a second transformer.
Heat is the first specification decision

Upper Egypt regularly designs to a 45 °C ambient. A charger that derates above 40 °C delivers its worst service exactly when demand peaks. Specify units that hold rated output at 45 °C, add shading and ventilation to the compound, and plan dust filters into the maintenance schedule — desert dust is a cooling problem before it is a cosmetic one.

Charging equipment enters Egypt through GOEIC conformity checks. Documents, nameplate data and test reports should be assembled before the equipment ships, not after it lands. Sequence the project as: connection offer, conformity file, then production — a site that waits on either of the first two pays for idle inventory.
faq: Who sets what EV drivers pay per kWh in Egypt?
The state does. Decision 101/2025 fixes the resale margin at the supply tariff plus 0.45 on AC and 0.80 on DC charging.
What ambient temperature should an Egyptian DC site be designed for?
45 °C is a practical design point for Upper Egypt. Chargers should hold rated output there instead of derating in the summer afternoon peak.
What must clear before chargers ship to Egypt?
GOEIC import conformity. The conformity file — nameplate data, test reports, documents — should be complete before equipment leaves the factory.

pages.title: EV Charging in Turkey: Licensing and Pricing Caps | Anari
pages.meta: Turkey's EV charging rules in one page: EPDK licensing, the 1 July 2026 motorway card-payment duty for 50 kW+ DC, and the 25% price cap over the best rate.
pages.h1: EV charging in Turkey: EPDK licensing, motorway payment rules, price caps
pages.lede: Turkey is one of the few markets where the charging business is licensed like a utility and priced like one too. The rules are explicit: an EPDK licence, card payment from 1 July 2026 on motorways, and a 25% ceiling over your own best rate.
pages.tldr: Charge point operators need an EPDK licence. From 1 July 2026, DC units of 50 kW and above on motorways must accept card payment. Prices may not exceed the operator's best rate by more than 25% anywhere in the network.
sections: The EPDK licence is the entry ticket, and the pricing rule that comes with it shapes the network design. Because no session may be priced more than 25% above the operator's best rate, price discrimination across locations is bounded — revenue strategy has to come from utilisation and uptime rather than from charging more at captive sites.
The motorway payment rule changes the hardware list

From 1 July 2026, DC chargers of 50 kW and above on motorways must accept card payment. That is a hardware and integration requirement, not a promise in an app: the payment terminal, its certification and its failover behaviour belong on the equipment checklist at procurement time, not at commissioning.
What we can quote for a Turkish site

The charging hardware, the ANARI OS backend and the service plan are quotable. Grid connection, civil works and the payment-terminal certification depend on the site and the licensed operator of record, which is why a survey precedes any number.
faq: Do EV charging operators need a licence in Turkey?
Yes. Charging networks are licensed by EPDK, the energy regulator, before commercial operation.
Which chargers must accept card payment on Turkish motorways?
DC units of 50 kW and above, from 1 July 2026 onward. The payment terminal is part of the equipment scope, not an app feature.
How is charging pricing capped in Turkey?
No session may cost more than 25% above the operator's own best rate, which limits location-based price discrimination.

pages.title: EV Charging in Morocco: Law 82-21 and Site Design | Anari
pages.meta: Building EV charging in Morocco: Law 82-21 self-production, the ONEE connection and the Tangier–Kenitra corridor, plus the Chergui wind factor in site design.
pages.h1: EV charging in Morocco: Law 82-21 self-production and the auto corridor
pages.lede: Morocco lets a site generate part of its own supply under Law 82-21, and the Tangier–Kenitra corridor concentrates the vehicles that need it. Both facts point at the same design: DC charging paired with on-site PV and storage.
pages.tldr: Law 82-21 opens a self-production route, ONEE remains the single national utility for the grid side, and the Tangier–Kenitra automotive corridor is where duty cycles justify DC power with PV plus storage on site.
sections: Under Law 82-21 a site can produce part of its own electricity. For a DC charging site that pairs naturally with rooftop or canopy PV plus a battery: the battery shaves the demand peaks that DC guns create, and the PV covers a share of daytime energy. The grid connection with ONEE is sized for the remainder, not for the full nameplate.

The Tangier–Kenitra axis carries Morocco's automotive industry and its fleet traffic. Corridor sites see predictable, repeated duty cycles — the profile where DC fast charging earns its capital cost — while city sites behave more like destination charging with lower, flatter demand.
Design for the Chergui, not for the brochure

The Chergui brings hot, dry, dust-laden wind off the Sahara. Enclosure filtering, sealing and a cleaning schedule are part of the specification in Morocco, exactly as 45 °C thermal design is in the Gulf — the climate sets the maintenance plan before the first session is sold.
faq: Can a Moroccan EV charging site produce its own power?
Yes. Law 82-21 provides a self-production route, which pairs well with on-site PV and battery storage behind the grid connection.
Who controls the grid connection in Morocco?
ONEE, the single national utility, handles the grid side; the site's connection offer sizes how much charger power can be served.
Which region justifies high-power DC first in Morocco?
The Tangier–Kenitra automotive corridor, where fleet duty cycles are repeated and predictable.
